subject: AP-Southeast autoscaler regression — SLO remedy request and expedited postmortem
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@stellara.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+platform@stellara.io
Date: Fri, 02 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AP-Southeast: repeated 503s since 02:55 UTC — need compensation & postmortem

Hi Rafael,

We saw a sustained spike of 503 responses affecting checkout requests from 02:55 UTC through ~03:38 UTC this morning in ap-southeast-1. Our telemetry shows ~23% failed checkout attempts during the window; downstream retries caused several orders to timeout and we had to fall back to a degraded routing plan.

Can you confirm Redwood's observed availability window, whether this qualifies under the SLO for downtime/availability credits, and provide an expedited postmortem? We're on a tight renewal timeline and need the remediation and credit estimate to brief procurement.

I've attached a sample trace bundle and a CSV of our metric rollup.

Attachments: trace_bundle_ap-southeast_090228.zip (application/zip), metric_snapshot_090228.csv (text/csv)

Thanks,
Amit Shah
Sr. Platform Ops, Stellara Payments
amit@stellara.io

Folks,

Amit just reported a 503 spike for Stellara in ap-southeast-1. I'm opening an incident (INF-4217) and will pull the autoscaler and routing events. Marcus, can you check the node eviction/scale events between 02:40–03:50 UTC? Laura, please capture the load balancer failure traces and any routing fallback logs.

- precise start/end of unavailable requests (per Redwood ingress)
- raw traces for representative requests (Amit attached sample — thanks)
- preliminary credit eligibility window for SLO team review (Hannah)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Amit Shah <amit@stellara.io>
Date: Fri, 02 Sep 2028 11:02:51 -0700
Subject: RE: AP-Southeast outage window — initial triage

Rafael / team,

Quick summary of what I can see so far (preliminary):
- At 02:47:58 UTC an orchestrated rollout to the autoscaler control plane triggered a scheduling regression on the ap-southeast GPU pool (known risky build, rolling back now).
- Several worker pods were briefly evicted between 02:48:10–03:04:37 UTC while the rollout failed; traffic was routed to a smaller standby pool which then experienced saturation and started returning 503s.
- Normal ingress acceptance resumes around 03:39:50 UTC once the rollback completed and caches warmed.

Prelim downtime window (Redwood ingress observed): 02:48:10 UTC — 03:39:50 UTC.

I've attached the raw autoscaler traces and the metric snapshot used to estimate the window. Pointed to INF-4217 for tracking.

Attachments: incident_playbook_snapshot.pdf (application/pdf), metric_snapshot_090228.csv (text/csv)

For credit calc: we need the tenant's observed failed requests, but the contractual SLO uses Redwood ingress accept rate — Hannah, can you confirm whether the 02:48–03:39 window would meet the threshold for a pro-rated credit under our SLA?

-Marcus
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
redwood.com

On Fri, Sep 2, 2028 at 09:34 AM Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@stellara.io>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Sep 2028 08:14:07 -0700
Subject: Redwood confirmation and next steps — ap-southeast incident (INF-4217)

Hi Amit,

Thanks again for the traces and metric snapshot — we've completed an initial validation of the incident. Below is our working summary and proposed next steps: 

Incident summary (prelim):
- A rollout to the autoscaler control plane caused a transient scheduling regression that evicted a subset of worker pods in ap-southeast-1.
- Traffic was routed to a smaller standby pool which became saturated and returned elevated 503s.
- Observed Redwood ingress failure window: 2028-09-02 02:48:10 UTC — 2028-09-02 03:39:50 UTC.

What we will deliver:
- Formal incident report / postmortem (detailed timeline, root cause, remediation, and mitigations) within five business days.
- Pro-rated SLO credit estimate for the affected window; preliminary calculation indicates a partial credit under Section 4.2 of our SLA. We'll provide the exact credit amount after correlating your tenant-level failed request counts to Redwood ingress metrics.
- A short-term mitigation plan (block the risky build and tighten Canary rollout rules) has been applied to prevent immediate recurrence.

Requested from you: billing contact and PO / invoice reference to apply any credit against.

I've attached the incident playbook snapshot we used in the triage and the metric CSV for transparency. If you want the postmortem sooner we can expedite but will need to prioritize engineering hours.

Attachments: incident_playbook_snapshot.pdf, metric_snapshot_090228.csv

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
